title: Count Cells in Overlapping Horizontal and Vertical Substrings
statement:
The input is a grid `grid` with `m` rows and `n` columns, each cell holding a lowercase letter, plus a string `pattern`.

- Reading the cells row by row (each row from left to right, the rows from top to bottom) produces one string of length `m * n`. Any occurrence of `pattern` in that string is a **horizontal match**. A match may run past the end of one row and carry on at the start of the next row, but the last row never continues into the first.
- Reading the cells column by column (each column from top to bottom, the columns from left to right) produces another string of length `m * n`. Any occurrence of `pattern` in it is a **vertical match**. A match may run past the bottom of one column and carry on at the top of the next column, but the last column never continues into the first.

Return how many cells are covered by at least one horizontal match and also by at least one vertical match. Matches may overlap each other.
constraints: grid and pattern contain only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Because a match may wrap onto the next row (or column), each direction is one flat string of length `m * n`: the row-by-row reading and the column-by-column reading. For each reading we need the positions inside some occurrence of `pattern`; after that every cell is a lookup. Comparing at every start costs O(m·n·|pattern|). KMP finds all occurrences in one linear pass, and a difference array marks the covered stretches.

## Approach

1. Build `lps`: `lps[i]` is the length of the longest proper prefix of `pattern[0..i]` that is also its suffix.
2. `coverage(text)` runs KMP: `matched` counts the pattern letters matched so far and falls back through `lps` on a mismatch.
3. When `matched` reaches `len`, an occurrence ends at `i`: add 1 at `diff[i - len + 1]`, subtract 1 at `diff[i + 1]`, and fall back to `lps[len - 1]` to keep finding overlapping matches.
4. The running sum `active` of `diff` is positive exactly on covered positions; store that in `covered`.
5. Build `rowText` and `colText`, get `inRow` and `inCol`, and count the cells `(r, c)` where `inRow[r * n + c]` and `inCol[c * m + r]` are both true.

## Example 1, step by step

`pattern = "abaca"` gives `lps = [0, 0, 1, 0, 1]`. The row reading `"aaccbbbcaabacaacaaba"` has one match, at indexes 9 to 13: cells (2,1), (2,2), (2,3), (3,0), (3,1). The column reading `"abacaabaaacbbabccaca"` has one match, at indexes 0 to 4: all of column 0. Only cell (3,0) is in both (row index 12, column index `0 * 5 + 3 = 3`), so the answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m·n + |pattern|): building `lps`, both scans and the final count are linear.
- Space: O(m·n + |pattern|) for the readings, their difference arrays and `lps`.

## Pitfalls

- Matching row by row misses matches that wrap; read the whole grid as one string per direction.
- In the column reading, cell `(r, c)` sits at `c * m + r`, not `r * n + c`.
- After a full match continue from `lps[len - 1]`, not 0, or overlapping matches such as `"aa"` in `"aaa"` are lost.
- Marking every letter of every match is O(m·n·|pattern|) on a grid of one letter; the difference array keeps it linear.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `m`, `n` | number of rows and columns |
| `len` | length of `pattern` |
| `lps`, `border` | the KMP table, and the prefix-suffix length while it is built |
| `matched` | pattern letters matched at the current position |
| `diff`, `active` | +1 at match starts and -1 just after match ends, and its running sum |
| `rowText`, `colText` | the grid read row by row and column by column |
| `inRow`, `inCol` | whether each position of those readings is inside a match |
| `count` | cells covered in both directions |
